summary: Halloween was a busy, mostly fun day. Mainstream collectors posted family rip sessions and Walmart restock hauls, while One Piece EB-05 came out and restock tracking was the main talk. On the crypto side, Collector Crypt got a lot of attention: a revenue list put it next to big crypto names, Blackboard launched Halloween packs powered by it, and a creator compared its $90 instant buyback to eBay and Courtyard payouts. Solflare Packs mentions were steady and positive, led by @Tukytuky_ and @diegoarmandoAD, with one angry reply calling the $69 packs a scam.

top_posts.text: I think I just found something the Pokémon card market hasn't caught onto yet. Some booster packs now have a calculated expected return of over 200%. Here's the math.
top_posts.why_it_matters: 18.9k impressions, the most-seen pack post of the day. Collectors are hungry for pack value math. We should not echo the 'return' framing, but showing odds clearly fits this interest.

top_posts.text: Halloween restock at Walmart!! @CardPurchaser insane they have all pokemon and One Piece plus all sports!!! What I bought below!
top_posts.why_it_matters: 18.3k impressions. Retail restocks are still big news for collectors, which shows how hard sealed product is to find.

top_posts.text: One Piece EB-05 Officially Released today. When it comes to One Piece releases the first two weeks are key as that is when they are the most consistent for restocks. You can check restock history for past One Piece releases here.
top_posts.why_it_matters: 14.7k impressions. New One Piece set means another round of restock chasing. Packs you can open any time answer that.

top_posts.text: Here's mine pulled this mew from celebrations and it's common. Seen loads of 'god' pulls on the timeline. It is possible but remember there are odds to check you can buy Pokemon cards too you want. Also tried collector crypt $50 Halloween packs which were decent.
top_posts.why_it_matters: 4.2k impressions. A mid-size Pokémon creator reminds people to check odds and tries Collector Crypt's Halloween packs. Odds shown up front is a message that lands.

top_posts.why_it_matters: 2.8k impressions. New, non-crypto collectors ripping packs as a social family moment. That is the mainstream audience we want.

top_posts.text: On a card insured at $100, a Collector Crypt machine pays $90 in USDC within seconds. An eBay sale leaves $86.35 after fees and before shipping, and Courtyard pays $84.60.
top_posts.why_it_matters: 823 impressions. Instant buyback is becoming the comparison point between platforms. Worth knowing for internal positioning, not for public copy.

sources_note: X search via the x connector, posts from 2026-10-31 09:00 UTC to 2026-11-01 09:00 UTC, 9 post searches and 1 X news search. Engagement numbers are copied from the X API at scan time. The Collector Crypt revenue figure is an unverified third-party claim; the Pokémon price drop item is an X news summary (Grok-written). @SolflareEmpire's top post was media-only, so its content is not described. Payments talk was thin: card, Apple Pay and wallet searches mostly returned memecoin and trading posts, which were skipped. Restock bots (PokeWatchCanada, packpingnet), eBay listing posts, referral-link promos, token shills (e.g. $SLABS) and repeated phygital NFT spam (SurRNFTs) were skipped. Creators already in collector-base.csv or earlier daily files were excluded. The 'which would you rather' idea needs real pulls chosen by the team; no odds or value claims are included.
